core_obligations: Set up the exact sequence (proof lines 5293-5305): the author writes the short exact sequence relating the derived limit to the limit and its first derived functor, and takes the long exact cohomology sequence at the object V.

Use the hypotheses (proof lines 5305-5317): hypothesis (1) kills the R^1 lim term over the members of the cofinal system of coverings, and hypothesis (2) identifies the relevant limit with the term at level n(V), which yields the injectivity of the map on sections.
proof_roadmap: Write the exact sequence relating the derived limit, the limit and R^1 lim.
Take cohomology at V and use the vanishing hypothesis to kill the R^1 lim contribution over a cofinal system of coverings.
Use the stability hypothesis to identify the limit with the term at level n(V), giving injectivity.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves an injectivity statement for the sections of a derived limit: under a vanishing hypothesis on R^1 lim of the cohomology of the system over a cofinal system of coverings, and a stability hypothesis in degree m, the map H^m(R lim K_n)(V) -> H^m(K_{n(V)})(V) is injective (statement lines 5278-5291). The proof writes the standard exact sequence relating the derived limit to the limit and R^1 lim (proof lines 5293-5305), and then uses the two hypotheses to kill the extra term and identify the limit with the term at the chosen level (proof lines 5305-5317). The non-formal content is the reading of the hypotheses in the exact sequence. The claim is H2: one exact sequence plus one application of the hypotheses.
